newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to lower bank reserve ratio to 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to lower bank reserve ratio to 5.5 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Korea said on Wednesday it would lower the reserve requirement ratio for South Korean banks by two percentage points to 5.5 percent, effective on November 8.
The cut in the proportion of deposits that banks must place as reserves with the central bank is effectively a move towards lower bank lending rates.
"We plan to lower the reserve requirement ratio to an average of 5.5 percent from November 8," a Bank of Korea official said.
The bank said it plans to cut its rediscount lending to banks to absorb the rise in liquidity stemming from a fall in the reserve ratio.

"The reserve base for banks is expected to rise by 2.6 trillion won as a result of the fall in the reserve requirement ratio. The rise will be absorbed by the reduction in the central bank's rediscount lending," the official said.
Details would be announced on Thursday, he added.
